messages:
ana: Heads-up — I measured a ~18% throughput regression on the MoE 8x-A100 serving job after the KV-cache change. Quick flamegraph shows a lot more small NCCL all-reduce calls coming from routing.

mike: Ugh. Is this the KV cache invalidation that touches per-token routing metadata?

ana: Yeah looks correlated. When we started flushing small KV slices on a per-request basis the routing tensors ended up split across micro-batches, producing many tiny all-to-all ops.

jyoti: Do you have the profiler traces? nvprof / Nsight?

ana: Pasted the critical snippet below (trimmed).

```
# nsight summary (trimmed)
Time breakdown (per-step):
 - compute kernels: 62ms
 - all-reduce / all-gather / all-to-all: 40ms (was ~20ms prior)
 - idle / NCCL sync: 18ms
 - memcpy / host: 4ms
```

Top NCCL calls were lots of `alltoall` on ~64 KB tensors, repeated ~50x per step. Before we had ~12 larger alltoall calls.

sam: So many small tensors -> poor NCCL utilization and startup latency dominates. Can we batch routing tensors into fewer larger messages?

leo: Also check that our pipeline/tensor parallel implementation isn't forcing a sync between routing and subsequent compute. There might be a stream dependency.

ana: Good call. I inspected stream usage and found we were doing `cudaStreamSynchronize` in the KV flush path when routing metadata is written back. That forces compute/comm serialization.

mike: Proposed immediate mitigations?

ana: Short term: 1) coalesce routing tensors in the runtime before issuing all-to-all (group by expert destination, pack into contiguous buffer). 2) avoid the KV-flush sync: move writes to a non-blocking stream and use event-based sync only before reading. 3) tweak batching heuristics to prefer slightly larger micro-batches when MoE routing is active.

jyoti: Medium term: update kernel selection to use a 'packed routing' kernel that outputs per-expert packed tensors, eliminating one copy and reducing number of NCCL calls. Also consider using NCCL groups to aggregate ops.

perf-bot: benchmark finished: baseline (pre-change) = 11.8k tok/s, current regressed = 9.6k tok/s.

sam: Good data. Ana, can you sketch a patch for coalescing before EOD? I can do the event/stream changes.

ana: I'll open a draft PR with a runtime pass that folds same-destination routing entries into a single buffer. Local microbench shows packing reduces all-to-all count from 48 -> 10 and theoretical comm time down ~2.5x. Patch inbound.

mike: Also let's add a perf test that runs 8x-A100 with synthetic routing skew so we can catch regressions earlier. Add an alert if all-to-all count > N per step.

leo: One more note: KV cache behavior for streaming completion — avoid small per-token RPCs that trigger cache updates. We'll aggregate cache writes for streaming clients. Might be a config knob in the short term.

jyoti: After coalescing + event-based async we should try overlap: launch all-to-all on stream 1, schedule L2/L3 compute on stream 0 that doesn't depend on routing outputs, then synchronize. If we can hide half the 40ms comm under compute we recover a lot.

ana: Agreed. I'll include a small roadmap in the PR: (a) immediate coalesce pack, (b) remove syncs and use events, (c) new packed routing kernel, (d) perf tests + alert.

sam: timeline works. I'll pair with Ana later for stream semantics.

perf-bot: Note: regression label added to ticket #INF-3221.

mike: Thanks. If anyone finds other regressions tied to the KV change, ping here. :thinking:

leo: Also adding an item to the ops runbook: how to run NCCL trace and interpret small-alltoall hotspots. I'll draft a short checklist.

ana: Thanks team — PR link when ready.
